content:
Hi everyone,

I’m looking to get started contributing to Rust for Linux, but the issue tracker is quite broad and I'd appreciate some guidance on a good entry point.

Background & Experience:

  • Experience writing kernel-level Rust in hobby projects.

  • Prior merged patches in the upstream C kernel tree.

  • Familiarity with the standard patch submission and review workflows.

Goal:

  • I'm looking for a beginner-friendly "good first issue" or small abstraction to implement.

  • Alternatively, I have a Galaxy Book 5 with missing upstream platform/driver support. I’m considering authoring Rust abstractions or platform driver modules for this hardware to expand device support while contributing upstream.

Does tackling platform/driver support for this hardware sound viable given the current state of tree abstractions, or would you recommend picking up existing low-hanging subsystem abstractions first? Any pointers to specific issues or relevant topics would be appreciated.

Thanks!

If you have hardware that is not supported by in-tree C drivers, then that is the best-case scenario to justify new Rust abstractions, plus it is usually fun to get it working -- I would say go for it! :)
